$comment: Attribution for the COMPILED BINARIES this image adds on top of exeuntu (story DF2.10, AC5).
DF2.9's package sweep walks a node_modules tree and can say nothing about an ELF; this table is
the substance that discharges the obligation for those. It is NOT the coverage set: the set of
binaries that must appear here is COMPUTED by scripts/build-exedev-image.ts, which enumerates the
executables in the built image, enumerates them in the base image, diffs, and refuses to tag when
an added binary has no entry below. A table asserted against a list the table itself supplies is
tautological and would pass on an image carrying an unattributed binary.
The diff is BY PATH AND CONTENT: a built executable is 'added' when the base image has no file at
that path OR the base's bytes at that path differ (both listings are sha256'd, and the comparison
is `baseBins.get(p) !== sha`). So a binary the base already ships at the same path but whose bytes
we re-pin — pi, which exeuntu itself installs and this image re-installs at PI_VERSION — IS flagged
and MUST be attributed here. The pin is ours, so the attribution is ours, and the gate now says so
rather than relying on us to remember.
COVERAGE IS BY PATH (issue #188, closed at DF1.10's re-pin). 'names' are the full in-image paths
the executable listing produces — no leading slash — and an added binary is covered when its path
is named, exactly. It used to be covered when its BASENAME was named, so /opt/vendor/bun read as
covered by a table that establishes oven-sh/bun at /usr/local/bin: attribution satisfiable by a
coincidence of names, in a gate whose diff had just been strengthened to catch content-level
replacement. The interim 'paths' narrowing is GONE rather than left in place — once a name IS a
path it could only restate or contradict it, and a field that reads as a safety narrowing while
doing nothing is worse than no field; validateBinaryLicenses REFUSES an entry that still carries
one. It also refuses a bare basename and refuses two entries claiming one path, because which of
them a basename match happened to win was an ordering accident that decided what the NOTICE said.
A re-pin that moves an install location must move these paths in the same change or the build
refuses to tag.
Every TOP-LEVEL entry's 'spdxId' must resolve to a canonical text in oci/license-texts/ (the
build validates this with DF2.9's own resolveLicenseText). 'UNVERIFIED' is a legal value there
and is a BUILD FAILURE by design: it is how an unestablished license is recorded honestly
instead of guessed at.
The rule stops at the top level, deliberately and not by oversight. validateBinaryLicenses
requires only 'component', 'url' and 'note' of a 'bundled' member and does NOT resolve its
spdxId — which is what lets the LGPL-2.0-or-later and NOASSERTION entries below exist while no
LGPL text is checked in. Widening the canonical-text set to statically-linked components is
DF4.1's sweep. Stated here because the unscoped version of this sentence read as a guarantee
the build does not make.
CORRECTION to an earlier version of this note, which claimed a top-level 'NOASSERTION' is not
enforced. It IS enforced, and the two sentences above and below cannot both have been true. It
simply refuses by the ORDINARY path rather than the 'UNVERIFIED' special case: there is no
NOASSERTION.txt in oci/license-texts/ (and there could not sensibly be one), so resolveLicenseText
returns null and validateBinaryLicenses reports 'no canonical text in oci/license-texts/ for
"NOASSERTION"'. Different message, same build failure. Both spellings of 'we do not know' stop a
publish at the top level; only a 'bundled' member may carry NOASSERTION, because its spdxId is
never resolved. Verified against scripts/build-exedev-image.ts validateBinaryLicenses and
scripts/lib/license-sweep.ts resolveLicenseText, 2026-09-01.
Every URL below is pinned to the TAG of the artifact this image ships, never to blob/main/ — a
table that argues against mutable references cannot cite them. 'verifiedAt' pins the observation;
the tag pins the target. The one exception is the WebKit pointer, which is a bare repository URL
because that is exactly what bun's own LICENSE.md gives at the pinned tag; substituting a ref we
invented would be a worse pointer than upstream's.

entries.verifiedHow: PROVENANCE: 1.3.13 is oci/exedev/Dockerfile's ARG BUN_VERSION default, itself read from package.json `packageManager` by readBunPin and passed as --build-arg by scripts/build-exedev-image.ts, which also pins ARG BUN_SHA256 for that release's bun-linux-x64.zip. The ARG is overridable with --build-arg, so this field states the version of the PINNED build; an override that moves it must move this entry in the same change. LICENCE: 2026-08-31, fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oven-sh/bun/main/LICENSE.md — first line reads 'Bun itself is MIT-licensed.'; npm view bun@1.3.13 license = MIT. 2026-09-01, re-fetched at the TAG the Dockerfile downloads from, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oven-sh/bun/bun-v1.3.13/LICENSE.md — same first line, and it is that document (not main's) that names the static-link graph disclosed under 'bundled'.
entries.notes: 'bunx' is deliberately NOT listed: the Dockerfile installs exactly one file (`install -m 0755 bun-linux-x64/bun /usr/local/bin/bun`) and creates no bunx symlink, so naming it here claimed attribution for a binary this image does not ship. The coverage direction was safe — uncoveredBinaries diffs added-against-covered, so a name with no binary is inert — but the table is the legal artifact and attributedBinaries publishes its claims. Nothing in src/ or scripts/ invokes bunx in-box; if that changes, add the symlink to the Dockerfile AND the name back here, in the same re-pin. bun is MIT, but the SHIPPED BINARY statically links components under other licenses; they are disclosed in 'bundled' below rather than folded into spdxId, because spdxId names the license of the project we redistribute and a single identifier cannot honestly carry a static-link graph. GitHub's license API reports NOASSERTION for this repo for the same reason: LICENSE.md is a composite document, not a bare MIT text.

bundled.note: A bare repository URL, and deliberately so: it is verbatim what bun's own LICENSE.md at tag bun-v1.3.13 gives ('You can find the patched version of WebKit used by Bun here: <https://github.com/oven-sh/webkit>'), verified 2026-09-01. Upstream publishes no per-release ref for it, and inventing one would point at bytes nobody claims are the ones linked in. LGPL-2 clause (1) requires that a recipient be able to relink the application against a modified library. Discharged by the upstream instructions in bun's LICENSE.md plus the patched-WebKit source at the URL above. No LGPL text is checked into oci/license-texts/ — widening the canonical-text set to statically-linked components is DF4.1's sweep, not this story's, and pretending otherwise would mean shipping a NOTICE entry with no text behind it (DF2.9 INV-4).

bundled.note: Enumerated with per-library licenses in bun's own LICENSE.md (MIT / BSD-3-Clause / several-licenses). Recorded as a pointer, not transcribed: a transcription drifts on the next bun bump and a stale transcription is a worse attribution than a live reference. The pointer is pinned to the TAG this image ships, not to blob/main/ — 'a live reference' meant a reference that still describes THESE bytes, and main's LICENSE.md will one day enumerate a different static-link graph. Re-pin it in the same change that moves BUN_VERSION.

entries.verifiedHow: PROVENANCE: 0.84.4 is oci/exedev/Dockerfile's ARG PI_VERSION default, installed by `exeuntu update pi --home /home/exedev --version`. The ARG is overridable with --build-arg, so this field states the version of the PINNED build; an override that moves it must move this entry in the same change. Unlike bun there is NO content check on that install (no upstream checksum to pin), so the build records the sha256 of the installed binary in /etc/qds-image.json as `piSha256` — a record for drift detection, not a verification. LICENCE: the compiled ELF is NOT the npm package: npm @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent stops at 0.73.1 and has no 0.84.4, so the 0.55.0 manifest's `license: MIT` does not establish this artifact. Established instead at the release channel exeuntu actually pulls from — GitHub release earendil-works/pi v0.84.4 ships pi-linux-x64.tar.gz (the standalone binary the DF1.10 probe measured at /usr/local/bin/pi), and that repository's root LICENSE, fetched the same day, is the MIT text with 'Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner' (GitHub license API: spdx_id MIT). 2026-09-01, re-fetched AT THE TAG rather than at main — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/v0.84.4/LICENSE opens 'MIT License' / 'Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner', and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v0.84.4 resolves; a nonexistent tag returns 404 on both, so the 200 is the tag and not a soft redirect to the default branch. 2026-09-10, PATH MOVED, LICENCE UNCHANGED: the base re-pinned at ea6c3f5c moved the ELF from /home/exedev/.local/bin/pi to /home/exedev/.local/pi/pi (measured from publish run 34534221743's build log — the added-binary diff refused on exactly that path, and `readlink -f /usr/local/bin/pi` resolved to it); the installed bytes are still the v0.84.4 release asset this entry already attributes (the build asserts `pi --version` = PI_VERSION), so the licence establishment above carries over and only the `names` path moves, per the table's own rule that a re-pin moving an install location moves these paths in the same change.
entries.notes: `names` keys on the path the AC5 added-binary diff (`find -type f`) actually produces — the real ELF file, never a symlink. That path has moved once already: 2026-09-01's build saw the ELF at /home/exedev/.local/bin/pi (then the regular file, with /usr/local/bin/pi the symlink); the 2026-09-10 base re-pin measured the ELF at /home/exedev/.local/pi/pi, with a leftover LINK at the old bin/pi path whose `-f`-through-the-link truth let the Dockerfile's old placement tie keep passing through the move (the tie now asserts the real ELF path and the symlink's exact target — see oci/exedev/Dockerfile's THREE PATHS note). Under path coverage (#188) a name no listing can ever produce attributes nothing, so the old path is not kept 'for safety': a second name would read as a second claim that had been checked.

entries.verifiedHow: PROVENANCE: this is FIRST-PARTY code. The file at this path is a two-line `/bin/sh` wrapper written by DF1.10's engine builder stage (`exec bun /opt/qds-factory/scripts/pipeline-run.ts "$@"`); the engine it execs is scripts/pipeline-run.ts and its src/ imports, shipped as UNBUNDLED SOURCE at /opt/qds-factory and interpreted by the pinned /usr/local/bin/bun attributed above. LICENCE: DECLARED, by the owner, in this change. This entry read `UNVERIFIED` — a deliberate build failure — for as long as the repository declared no licence at all. It now declares one: QDS-Factory is private, proprietary software, and the declaration lives in three places that must move together — the root `LICENSE` file, package.json `"license": "LicenseRef-QDS-Proprietary"` (alongside, not instead of, `"private": true`), and the canonical text at oci/license-texts/LicenseRef-QDS-Proprietary.txt, which is byte-identical to the root LICENSE and is what `resolveLicenseText` resolves this identifier against. `LicenseRef-` is the SPDX form for a licence with no SPDX-listed identifier, which is what a first-party proprietary licence is; `parseLicenseExpression` treats it as an ordinary atom and the lookup is case-insensitive, so no validator change was needed. NOT `NOASSERTION` and not an OSS identifier, deliberately: NOASSERTION means 'could not establish', which is false for code whose owner is the one filling in this field and would corrupt the two entries above that use it with that exact meaning for third-party artifacts; an OSS identifier would grant rights the owner is not granting. THE FILE IS A NOTICE, NOT THE COMMERCIAL GRANT — the agreement customers buy under is a separate EULA/MSA, and nothing in this table should be read as that grant. Not reviewed by counsel.
entries.notes: `bundled` IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and that is a CORRECTION made in the same change that moved the delivery route — not an omission. This entry used to disclose statically linked LGPL-2.0-or-later JavaScriptCore and bun's further static libraries, and while the engine shipped as a `bun build --compile` executable that was exactly right: a compiled bun executable EMBEDS the bun runtime, so that file really did redistribute the whole static-link graph and really did carry LGPL-2 clause (1)'s relink obligation. DF1.10 took AC2a's fallback route (see the route note in oci/exedev/Dockerfile: bundling collapses `import.meta.dir` to a single value and the engine's closure has two consumers needing different bases), so the file at this path is now a two-line shell script. A shell script embeds nothing. Leaving the disclosure would have been a FALSE CLAIM — attributing to a 90-byte wrapper a relink obligation it cannot discharge and does not incur — and a false attribution is not the safe direction just because it names more licences. The obligation did not disappear: it moved to the artifact that actually carries it, /usr/local/bin/bun, whose own entry above still discloses JavaScriptCore and the static libraries in full. Verify both together; they were one claim split across two files and must stay consistent. WHAT THIS PATH DOES NOT COVER: the engine's own source tree at /opt/qds-factory ships 0644 and non-executable, so it never enters the added-binary diff — it is first-party text from this repository and rides this same licence decision. Its third-party runtime closure (yaml, zod) ships at /opt/qds-factory/node_modules and is attributed by DF2.9's filesystem SWEEP and the generated NOTICE, not by this table: this table attributes BINARIES, the sweep attributes npm packages, and folding either into the other would put a claim in a place its own validator does not check.
